title: UV-Centered Quarter-Wave Stack for Maximum Excitation Suppression
scientific_hypothesis: A quarter-wave stack centered at 355 nm will achieve deeper UV stopband suppression than visible-centered designs, but at the cost of increased passband ripple in the 420-700 nm region.
design_principle: Bragg reflection condition: alternating high/low index layers with optical thickness λ/4 at the target stopband wavelength creates constructive interference for reflection. Centering at 355 nm maximizes reflectance at the excitation wavelength.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 36 layers, initialized near 355 nm quarter-wave condition (Ta2O5 ~62 nm, SiO2 ~95 nm), tuned during optimization
soft_objectives: keep individual layer thicknesses within 20-350 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Ta2O5/SiO2 material pair has known thermal stress behavior per L28
ion beam sputtering deposition recommended per L21
theory_basis: Quarter-wave Bragg stack theory for high-reflectance mirrors
Photonic crystal bandgap formation in 1D periodic structures
expected_advantages: Strongest UV stopband suppression among the three routes
known_risks: Visible passband may show significant ripple due to stopband edges
NIR stopband at 1030-1080 nm may be weaker as it relies on higher-order reflection
36 layers may increase thermal stress per L28
execution_request_english: Design a 36-layer periodic dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees, unpolarized light. Stack structure: Air | (Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Gao)) repeated 18 times | Fused Silica. Initialize layer thicknesses near quarter-wave condition at 355 nm (Ta2O5 (Gao) approximately 62 nm, SiO2 (Gao) approximately 95 nm based on typical refractive indices). Optimize all 36 individual layer thicknesses within 20-350 nm bounds to minimize average transmittance in 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm bands while maximizing average transmittance in 420-700 nm band. Report final layer thickness sequence and transmittance spectra across 350-1100 nm.
